summary: On Saturday, District Judge Darrin Gayles dismissed President Donald Trump 's lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal with prejudice, permanently barring the president from refiling claims over reporting on an alleged birthday letter to Jeffrey Epstein.

Trump filed the $10 billion defamation suit last year challenging The Wall Street Journal's 2025 report about a sexually suggestive letter in a 2003 album compiled for Epstein's 50th birthday, which Trump consistently denied writing.

Gayles determined Trump failed to prove 'actual malice,' the legal standard for defamation, finding the president's allegations were 'conclusory, vague' and often irrelevant to whether Defendants knew the statements were purportedly false.

The Supreme Court's landmark ruling in The New York Times v Sullivan establishes that Trump's arguments ran afoul of the First Amendment, with Gayles adding the president has been 'grasping at straws' to prove his case.

After serving as a British military major and privateer, Jones transitioned to colonial life in New York. In 1696, his father-in-law Thomas Townsend gifted him significant Long Island land, enabling a fresh start.

Colonial governor Richard Coote investigated Jones in 1698 after witness depositions reported a "barrel of money" reaching his home. Jones, described as "formerly a pirate," testified he knew nothing about the funds.

Maritime history professor Richard Blakemore cautions findings are "compelling but shouldn't be considered conclusive." Kevin McDonald notes such ties illustrate how piracy provided "foundational and multi-generational wealth" for Northeast families.

A 1906 family history by descendant Thomas Floyd-Jones dismissed pirate tales as "slander" and "improbable fictions." Recent research reveals early British colonies were deeply connected to piracy both socially and economically.
title: Iconic New York figure was likely "major player" in murderous pirate's 1695 heist, historian says

summary: On Monday, Marvell Technology announced it is buying optical components maker Lumentum in a $115 billion all-stock deal, aiming to challenge rival Broadcom and capitalize on the AI spending boom.

"Infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity," said Marvell CEO Matt Murphy, who will remain chairman and CEO of the combined company. The deal expands the company's total addressable market to $550 billion.

Big Tech's AI spending boom drives demand for optical components used to move data at high speeds. Reflecting this confidence, AI chip giant Nvidia invested $2 billion each in Marvell and Lumentum earlier this year.

To challenge Broadcom, the deal integrates Lumentum into Marvell's portfolio. Since talks were reported late last month, Lumentum's shares have fallen about 8% and Marvell about 22%, as a broad-based chip selloff accelerated following Intel's weak forecast.

Marvell expects the interconnect market to grow 65% a year to $65 billion by 2030, fueling long-term demand. The transaction, unanimously approved by both boards, is expected to close in the first half of calendar 2028.
title: Marvell to buy Lumentum in $115 billion deal in AI data-center bet

summary: On Sunday, Iran awaited a U.S. response to its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days, a day after President Donald Trump told reporters negotiations were "going fine" but that Iran was "not very reliable."

The blockade has severely restricted traffic through the waterway, with the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations center logging over 30 reported attacks in October, the highest of any month in the war, leaving the strait carrying only a fraction of prewar volume.

Iranian state media displayed missiles and drones on November 1, signaling an "immediate, effective response, without geographical limitations," while President Trump claimed American forces could handle "one or two sites" in Iran's nuclear program in 10 minutes.

Despite diplomatic signaling, violence persisted on the water over the weekend, as the Revolutionary Guard continued to enforce its own rules and at least four tankers were identified as struck on Friday and Saturday.

President Trump has set the U.S. midterm elections as the boundary for any resumption of strikes, with U.S. officials indicating strike options will be presented to him after the vote, establishing a critical deadline for negotiations.
title: Iran Has a 2-Day Plan to Reopen Strait, Resume Nuclear Talks with US, and Other Mideast News

summary: The Justice Department on Sunday asked District Court Chief Judge James Boasberg to consider contempt charges against an immigrant rights group after they published an analysis of a list containing more than 20,000 alleged noncitizen voters in California.

On Friday, Boasberg allowed the Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights access to federal government data to argue their legal standing, ordering the group not to disclose names and use the information only for court arguments.

Attorneys for the Coalition filed papers Saturday revealing their analysis found more than 40% of the people on the list do not appear in California's voter file, while identifying 22 people likely to be naturalized citizens.

Alberto Lammers, a spokesman for the Voting Rights Project, stated that counsel and experts "fully complied with the Court's orders," while the Justice Department argued the analysis was "political grandstanding" irrelevant to the group's legal standing.

Separately, the Justice Department appealed a ruling by District Court Judge Trina Thompson that barred the government from demanding election offices separate ballots or threaten legal action, with a hearing scheduled for Monday.

summary: On Saturday, the Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog mission 2 crew—Ross Elder, Ellen Ellis, Matthew Montgomery, and James Spicer—will emerge from their 378-day simulation at Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas.

Since October 2025, the crew lived within a 158-square-metre habitat to study how isolation, distance, and 'Mars-like' communication delays affect humans preparing for deep space missions to the Red Planet.

Crew members performed routine medical tasks including self-blood draws and heavy exercise throughout the mission. Volunteer Montgomery noted, "You can kind of see the finish line coming," as the assignment neared completion.

Following the mission, the crew will undergo two weeks of post-mission evaluations while reuniting with families they contacted only via email during the year-long assignment. Ellis expressed anticipation, saying, "Seeing my husband smile at me when the egress door opens."

Data from this mission will inform NASA 's Human Research Program on requirements for future long-duration moon base and Mars voyages, according to chief scientist Michael Stenger. NASA is currently accepting applications for the next simulation.
title: Crew from NASA's simulated Mars mission emerges after 378 days in isolation

summary: On Saturday, Director Michael Mann was hospitalized after accidentally shooting himself in the leg at The Range, a Los Angeles shooting facility. The 83-year-old filmmaker was reportedly attempting to holster his firearm when the weapon discharged.

Police classified the incident as a "training accident ," confirming that Mann did not purposely shoot himself. Authorities stated he was "injured during a training accident when he accidentally discharged a firearm into his own leg."

The incident occurred at The Range, a members-only club in Los Angeles with annual memberships ranging from around $3,000 to $20,000. Both LAPD and Los Angeles Fire Department personnel responded to the scene.

Mann is currently working on a long-awaited prequel to Heat with an all-star cast. Variety reported last month that Leonardo DiCaprio, Christian Bale, Adam Driver, Jason Clarke, and Odessa Young have joined the production.
The filmmaker has directed major titles since the 1980s, including Manhunter and the 2023 release Ferrari. Mann also published the #1 New York Times best-seller Heat.
title: Director Michael Mann Hospitalized After Shooting Himself at L.A. Gun Range: Reports

summary: On Monday, Anthropic filed to sell up to $3.5 billion worth of shares in Japan as part of its IPO, according to a regulatory filing.
The share sale targets a Japanese market that hit a 14-year low for first-time offerings, with proceeds funding working capital and operating expenses.
Mizuho Financial Group will manage the Japanese portion, while Goldman Sachs Group, Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities, and Morgan Stanley MUFG Securities handle investor orders.
Investors in Australia, Canada, and parts of Europe, apart from Japan, will also access the initial share sale of the Claude chatbot maker.
Anthropic's IPO will test investor appetite alongside equity financing from Alphabet and Meta Platforms, as some investors have discussed a valuation of about $1.5 trillion for the company.
title: Anthropic releases amended IPO prospectus with third-quarter financials

summary: On Sunday, November 1, Today show co-host Savannah Guthrie renewed her plea for information regarding her 84-year-old mother, Nancy Guthrie , who disappeared from her Catalina Foothills home in Tucson, Arizona, nine months ago.

The Pima County Sheriff's Department and FBI confirmed on Friday, October 30, that no suspects have been named, despite investigators recently traveling to Florida to consult lab scientists regarding DNA analysis.

Investigators continue to chase leads, including security footage of a masked man and several ransom notes, while the family maintains a $1 million reward for information leading to Nancy's discovery.
Savannah shared a drawing by her daughter on Instagram, writing the family "cannot move forward" until they discover what happened to Nancy, noting the disappearance has changed them forever.
Authorities urge the public to share information, emphasizing that "no tip is too small" to resolve the unsolved case, while the FBI maintains a separate $100K reward for relevant details.
title: ‘Please help us’: Savannah Guthrie issues new plea for help in mother’s kidnapping

summary: On Friday, Thomas Markle Sr, 82, transferred to a Florida facility specializing in "memory care" amid an ongoing FBI investigation into alleged child abuse material.

Federal investigators launched a probe after reports identified a storage unit in Rosarito, Mexico, allegedly containing child abuse images linked to Markle, with convictions potentially carrying 12 years in jail.
Characterizing the claims as "sick lies," Markle rejected the report on Saturday, telling The Mail, "I had no storage units in Rosarito."
Spencer Kuvin, a Florida-based lawyer, warned that Markle's "cognitive issues" could prevent police from conducting formal interviews at the new facility.

Meghan Markle described herself as "deeply distressed" by the allegations, while The Independent Office for Police Conduct investigates why British officers failed to escalate a 2019 letter regarding her father.
title: Meghan Markle's Father Moves to Dementia Care Home

summary: On Sunday, November 1, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed raised more than $2.4 million, his campaign's largest fundraising day, following Congresswoman Haley Stevens' endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers.
Congresswoman Haley Stevens' decision to endorse Rogers sparked significant backlash among Democrats, failing to attract new support for Rogers while unifying voters behind El-Sayed.
ActBlue rankings show El-Sayed moved to second place on the platform, outperforming established fundraising juggernauts Texas Senate candidate James Talarico and Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff.
Senator Elissa Slotkin and Governor Gretchen Whitmer signaled disapproval of the endorsement on social media, emphasizing that voters remain focused on economic concerns rather than political drama.
With Election Day approaching on Tuesday, November 3, the Michigan Senate race remains defined by voter frustration over economic issues as residents prepare to decide the state's representation.
title: El-Sayed Campaign Says It Raised Record $2.4 Million In One Day After Stevens GOP Endorsement

All perspectives acknowledge the 10-day operation, withdrawal, displacement, and continuing security activity, reflecting the broader conflict over occupation versus counterterrorism.
summary: On Monday, Israeli forces withdrew from Hebron in the West Bank after a 10-day siege, allowing displaced families to return to their homes.
The siege began October 23 following a shooting attack that killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three others; Israeli forces later killed the two attackers.
More than 3,300 Palestinians were displaced or otherwise affected, particularly in Al-Jalda and Ein Deir Baha, while the Hebron Governorate reported 15 homes and other structures were demolished.
Palestinian security forces have taken full control of the area, and Governor Khaled Dudin announced authorities are working to provide conditions for residents to return safely.
The Hebron Governorate stated the operation disrupted education and caused extensive damage to infrastructure and the local economy, compounding the humanitarian toll.
title: Israeli troops withdraw from Hebron after 10-day siege, governor says

summary: On Thursday, Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi , D-Calif., criticized New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed over their views on Israel, calling their positions "wrong."
The exchange occurs amid ongoing debates within the Democratic Party regarding Israel, particularly following the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks and the subsequent war in Gaza.

El-Sayed has faced scrutiny for describing Israel's war in Gaza as "genocide" and characterizing military actions as "bloodthirsty," while Mamdani has questioned support for states privileging one religion over others.
Pelosi responded that these positions are "more than concerning" and do not reflect the views of Democrats in Congress, stating that members would disassociate themselves from such rhetoric.
Running against Republican Mike Rogers for a Senate seat in a state Trump carried in 2024, El-Sayed has rejected claims that criticism of Israel is antisemitic, citing a commitment to Jewish safety.
title: Nancy Pelosi Criticizes Mamdani and El-Sayed Over Their Positions on Israel

summary: On Monday, the Crown withdrew all criminal charges against 44 pro-Palestinian protesters arrested during an April 2024 sit-in at a downtown Montreal Scotiabank, officially ending the prosecution.
Protesters occupied the branch demanding Scotiabank divest from Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit Systems, a move the bank eventually completed, which activists welcomed as a victory.

While 14 individuals previously pleaded guilty to municipal noise bylaw violations and paid $300 fines, defense lawyer Barbara Bedont noted most other protesters resolved their cases through community service.
Defendants challenged the charges under the Charter, arguing police violated their rights, and filed a formal complaint against the presiding judge alleging bias and unfair treatment.
Defense counsel Bedont warned that criminalizing peaceful sit-ins threatens the right to protest, suggesting the group's legal strategy likely influenced the Crown's decision to drop charges.
title: No Criminal Charges for Montreal Protesters Arrested at Bank Sit-In

summary: President Donald Trump returned to the campaign trail on Sunday and is scheduled to deliver a closing pitch at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington, less than 24 hours before polls open.
Early voting has shattered records this year, with the University of Florida Election Lab reporting more than 54 million ballots cast, nearly 9 million more than in the previous midterms.

Nationally, 43% of early votes came from registered Democrats and 32% from Republicans. Brookings Institution senior fellow Darrell West explained, "Typically, people vote when they think their vote matters."

Trump visited Kansas and Iowa, where the Cook Political Report considers Senate races "toss-ups." Historically, midterms challenge the president's party, and Republicans face difficulties maintaining control of both chambers.
Voters will decide all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats in the election. The Cook Political Report predicts Senate races in Ohio, Alaska, and Maine could go either way.
title: What does the surge in early voting mean for this midterm election?

summary: Two oil tankers struck naval mines while traveling an "unauthorized route" in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy reported, causing explosions that immobilized both vessels and ignited one.

Iran has enforced strict transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began in February, attacking vessels it claims violate navigation regulations to assert control over the strategic waterway.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations issued a security alert after a merchant vessel reported being struck by an "unknown projectile," though it remains unclear whether this incident links to the IRGC Navy report.
Following the explosions, both vessels remain immobilized, while the IRGC Navy warned that any "provocative action" in surveillance areas will be met with a "decisive and proportionate response."
The IRGC accused the two tankers of disabling navigation systems to transit clandestinely with alleged U.S. military support, part of a broader pattern of maritime incidents since the conflict began.
